results.input: Tell me about the world of Nox: how does its magic work? And what does Kael Draven carry?
results.answer:
Your lore does not mention a world called Nox. The world described in your canon is Aethel. Magic in Aethel is a mana-based system with three disciplines—Fire, Frost, and Aether [eac3e3c8]. The rules changed after the Sundering catastrophe, when mana rose to the surface and magic became accessible to anyone born with a mana pool [949896d6].

Is Nox a place within Aethel, or a different world you're developing? If you can clarify, I can search more specifically for its magic system.
evidence:
[search_lore] passage 935211ae (The Magic of Aethel): Magic in Aethel is paid for in mana. Every spell has a price, every caster has a limited pool, and the places of the world bend the rules in their own ways. This document lists the general laws. Individual places add their own rules, which are described in the location documents.
[search_lore] passage 43a85e83 (The Glass Library > Rules of the Library > Magic inside the Library): All magic is silenced inside the Glass Library, except for spells cast by a sworn Archivist. The glass walls absorb every working of every discipline, so a visitor who tries to cast a spell inside the Library simply feels the mana drain away with no effect. A spellbook can be read inside the Library, but nothing can be cast from it.
[search_lore] passage d217db3d (Ember Keep > Rules of the Keep > Frost magic in Ember Keep): Frost magic costs double mana inside Ember Keep. The heat of the volcano pushes against every working of the Frost discipline, so a frost lance that costs 15 mana anywhere else costs 30 mana inside the Keep. Fire magic is not affected, and it costs the normal price.

[search_lore] passage 935211ae (The Magic of Aethel): Magic in Aethel is paid for in mana. Every spell has a price, every caster has a limited pool, and the places of the world bend the rules in their own ways. This document lists the general laws. Individual places add their own rules, which are described in the location documents.
[search_lore] passage 949896d6 (History and Factions of Aethel > The Sundering): The Sundering was the catastrophe that broke the old world. In a single night the sky split, the central plains were fused into glass, and mana rose close to the surface of the land, where it had never been before. Before the Sundering, magic was a craft for a few scholars. After it, anyone born with a pool of mana could cast.

The Sundering also changed the price of magic. Teleportation, which had cost 30 mana before the Sundering, cost 50 mana after it, because the same journey now had to cross land that the Sundering had made unstable. The fields of fused glass are still there, and the Glass Library was built on them.
[search_lore] passage eac3e3c8 (The Magic of Aethel > The Three Disciplines): There are three disciplines of magic. Fire, also called pyromancy, creates and shapes flame and heat. Frost, also called cryomancy, creates and shapes ice and cold. Aether covers everything that works on distance and boundaries: teleportation, wards and scrying.

A minor spell of any discipline costs between 5 and 15 mana. A fire bolt costs 12 mana and a frost lance costs 15 mana. Greater workings, such as summoning a storm, cost far more and are limited to Archmages.

judge.reasoning: The answer says the lore does not mention Nox and identifies the world as Aethel. Each claim about Aethel is supported: magic runs on mana and there are three disciplines (eac3e3c8, 935211ae), and after the Sundering mana rose and anyone with a mana pool could cast (949896d6). The answer never mentions Kael Draven, which is an omission and not a faithfulness problem. Constraint 1 asks it to say it cannot find Kael Draven OR that the lore does not cover Nox. The second option is met. Constraint 2 holds: the answer describes Aethel's magic, not Nox's, and invents nothing about Kael.
